edges.analysis: Paper A leverages Paper B’s observational discoveries and empirical constraints—particularly the universal irradiation efficiency range (10%–30%) and companion filling factors—to establish the physical context and key parameters for its theoretical evolutionary models. By grounding its MESA-based simulations in these observed phenomena, Paper A uses Paper B as foundational background to investigate how irradiation efficiency dictates the divergent formation pathways of black widows and redbacks.

Paper A directly builds upon the observational baseline and initial findings established in Paper B, specifically leveraging the measured large positive orbital period derivative ($\dot{P}_{orb}$) and the preliminary connection to black widow binaries. Using these foundational results, Paper A develops a detailed physical model to explain the anomalous orbital evolution through quiescent mass ejection and highly non-conservative mass transfer.
